tlPageHero.label: TAX & LEGAL
tlPageHero.title: When Business Crosses Borders, Every Decision Has More Than One Dimension.
tlPageHero.description: Tax and legal considerations influence how businesses invest, operate, employ people, structure transactions and enter new markets.
tlPageHero.aside: As organisations expand internationally, those considerations become interconnected. A decision made in one jurisdiction can create tax, regulatory or commercial consequences elsewhere.

buttons.label: Discuss a Tax or Legal Matter

tlLocal.imageAlt: Advisers meeting in a modern office
tlLocal.text: Parker Russell member firms provide tax and legal expertise across international markets, combining knowledge of local requirements with the wider perspective needed when businesses, transactions, people and capital move across borders.
tlLocal.body: From day-to-day compliance to complex international structures and transactions, our professionals focus on understanding not only the immediate requirement — but the wider business context surrounding it.

rightColumn.text: Local rules matter. So does understanding how they connect.

tlJurisdictions.title: One Business Decision Can Trigger Questions Across Multiple Jurisdictions.

cards.title: Entering a New Market
cards.description: Expansion can create questions around corporate presence, taxation, operating structures, employees, transactions and local compliance.

cards.title: Operating an International Group
cards.description: Businesses with entities in several jurisdictions need to consider how activities, profits, transactions and obligations interact across the wider group.

cards.title: Moving People Across Borders
cards.description: International executives and mobile employees can create personal, corporate and reporting considerations in more than one jurisdiction.

cards.title: Buying or Selling a Business
cards.description: M&A can create significant tax consequences around transaction structure, ownership, financing and the treatment of assets or entities involved.

cards.title: Moving Goods Internationally
cards.description: Cross-border supply chains bring indirect tax, customs and trade considerations into everyday commercial operations.

cards.title: Changing the Corporate Structure
cards.description: Reorganisation, investment and changes in ownership can create consequences that need to be considered before the structure changes — not after.

tlExpertise.title: Expertise Across the Tax Questions International Business Creates.

cards.title: International Corporate Tax
cards.description: International businesses need to understand how tax rules interact across the jurisdictions in which they operate.
cards.descriptionSecondary:
Parker Russell member firms advise on international corporate tax matters, bringing local tax knowledge into the wider context of group structures, cross-border activities and commercial objectives.

The objective is not simply to address an isolated tax question, but to understand how decisions in one market may affect the wider organisation.

cards.title: Transfer Pricing
cards.description: Transactions between related entities are increasingly important to international tax management and regulatory scrutiny.
cards.descriptionSecondary:
Parker Russell professionals provide transfer pricing expertise around the policies, arrangements and documentation governing transactions between associated businesses.

Where multiple jurisdictions are involved, the ability to connect local requirements with the wider group position becomes particularly important.

cards.title: Mergers & Acquisitions
cards.description: Tax can materially influence the economics and structure of a transaction.
cards.descriptionSecondary:
Understanding relevant tax implications before an acquisition, disposal or restructuring can allow decision-makers to assess the transaction with a more complete view of its potential consequences.

Parker Russell member firms provide tax expertise around M&A matters in their relevant markets and can collaborate where transactions cross jurisdictions.

cards.title: Indirect Tax
cards.description: VAT and other forms of indirect taxation can affect pricing, cash flow, supply chains and compliance obligations.
cards.descriptionSecondary: For businesses operating internationally, different rules and reporting requirements can add considerable complexity to transactions that may appear commercially straightforward.

cards.title: Trade & Customs
cards.description: Moving goods across borders introduces customs, duties and other trade considerations that can influence cost, supply chains and operating decisions.
cards.descriptionSecondary: Understanding these obligations is particularly important when businesses enter new markets, change sourcing arrangements or reorganise international supply chains.

cards.title: International Executive Services
cards.description: International mobility can create tax and reporting considerations for both individuals and the organisations employing them.
cards.descriptionSecondary: Parker Russell's existing international tax offering includes International Executive Services, providing relevant expertise where executives and other individuals work across jurisdictions.

cards.title: e-Tax Solutions
cards.description: Technology continues to change the way tax information is prepared, reported and managed.
cards.descriptionSecondary: e-Tax Solutions form part of Parker Russell's established tax proposition, reflecting the increasing role of technology within tax administration and compliance.

cards.title: Domestic Business & Personal Tax
cards.description: International capability begins with strong local expertise.
cards.descriptionSecondary: Parker Russell member firms also provide domestic business and personal tax services according to the requirements and tax regimes of their respective jurisdictions.

tlEnvironments.title: One Organisation. Many Tax Environments.
tlEnvironments.secondaryLead: A group may operate commercially as one organisation while being treated differently by tax authorities across multiple jurisdictions.
tlEnvironments.emphasis:
The challenge is therefore not simply understanding each jurisdiction individually.
It is understanding how the jurisdictions interact around the same business.

network.text: Through Parker Russell International, independent member firms can collaborate where tax matters extend across borders, allowing relevant local expertise to contribute to a wider international perspective.

tlStructure.title: Structure Creates Consequences.
questions: Where should an international activity sit?
How should transactions between related entities be structured and documented?
What happens when capital, goods or people cross borders?
How will an acquisition affect the wider group?
What tax consequences could arise before profits are distributed?
Which obligations are created when a business enters another jurisdiction?
tlStructure.questionsNote: These questions demonstrate why tax should not be considered only at the end of a business decision.

stages.label: STRUCTURE

stages.label: TRANSACT

stages.label: OPERATE

stages.label: MOVE

stages.label: CHANGE

tlStructure.conclusion: Tax follows the business. Strong advice anticipates where it will lead.

tlRisk.title: Tax Risk Often Appears Where Business Complexity Meets Change.
tlRisk.lead: Tax exposure does not arise only from an incorrect calculation.
texts: It can arise because the business has changed while its tax position has not been reconsidered.
The earlier these implications are understood, the more effectively they can be addressed.
tlRisk.statement: The right time to understand a tax consequence is before it becomes a tax problem.

items.title: An employee begins working in another country.
A group introduces new intercompany arrangements.
An acquisition changes the corporate structure.
Digital activity creates obligations in markets where the organisation previously had limited presence.

tlKnowledge.eyebrow: FROM LOCAL RULES TO INTERNATIONAL PERSPECTIVE
tlKnowledge.title: International Tax Requires Local Knowledge.
tlKnowledge.lead: There is no single international tax system.

principles.text: Businesses operate within national legislation, local administrative requirements and different regulatory environments, while international treaties and cross-border principles can influence how those systems interact. Parker Russell's existing proposition explicitly identifies national and international tax laws, policies, accounting and commercial principles and international tax treaties as part of the knowledge required for its tax work.

That makes local expertise essential.
But when the business operates internationally, local answers must also be understood within the context of the wider organisation.

tlKnowledge.photoStatement: Local knowledge provides the answer in the jurisdiction. International collaboration helps reveal what that answer means elsewhere.

steps.label: OPERATE

steps.label: EXPAND

steps.label: INVEST
steps.description: Understanding the tax implications surrounding investment and M&A activity.

steps.label: RESTRUCTURE
steps.description: Considering the consequences of changes in ownership, operations or group structure.

steps.label: TRANSITION
steps.description: Addressing tax matters arising when assets or businesses are sold or ownership changes.

tlTogether.title: Tax and Legal Questions Often Meet at the Same Decision.

principles.text: International business decisions rarely fall neatly into one professional category. Corporate structures, transactions, ownership, contracts and market entry can involve legal considerations alongside taxation.
Where relevant capabilities are available within the network, Parker Russell member firms can bring appropriate tax and legal perspectives to matters requiring more than one discipline.

tlTogether.statement: For international businesses, this can provide a more connected understanding of the commercial decision and the requirements arising within the relevant jurisdictions.

tlIndustry.conclusion: Understanding the commercial and sector context therefore matters when interpreting how tax rules apply to the business itself.

tlFinal.ariaLabel: Think beyond the immediate tax question
tlFinal.title: Think Beyond the Immediate Tax Question.
tlFinal.description: A decision made today can create tax consequences across entities, transactions and jurisdictions long after it has been implemented.
tlFinal.note: Understanding those consequences early provides businesses with a stronger basis for deciding how to structure, invest, operate and expand. Parker Russell member firms combine local tax expertise with international collaboration to bring greater clarity to tax matters wherever business takes you.
tlFinal.tagline: Understand the rules locally. Understand the consequences internationally.
